question.problem:
Given that $L\{{e}^{at}\}=\frac{1}{s-a}$ for $s>a$, find the Laplace transform of
$g(t)={\int }_{0}^{t}{e}^{3τ}\,\text{d}τ$
for $s>3.$
question.worked_solution:
We know that if $L\{f(t)\}=F(s)$, then

$$
L\{{\int }_{0}^{t}f(τ)\,\text{d}τ\}=\frac{F(s)}{s}.
$$

In our case, $f(t)={e}^{3t}.$ Thus, for $s>3,$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(s) & =L\{f(t)\} \\  & =L\{{e}^{3t}\} \\  & =\frac{1}{s-3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, applying the integral identity above, we have that for $s>3,$

$$
\begin{aligned}L\{g(t)\} & =L\{{\int }_{0}^{t}{e}^{3τ}\,\text{d}τ\} \\  & =\frac{F(s)}{s} \\  & =\frac{1}{s(s-3)}.\end{aligned}
$$
